subject: Neurology
vignette: A 42-year-old man with early Parkinson disease is started on pramipexole. His physician explains that non-ergot dopamine agonists are preferred in younger patients. Several weeks later his wife reports that he has developed an uncontrollable urge to gamble and has had episodes of orthostatic dizziness and visual hallucinations.
question: Which of the following best describes pramipexole and ropinirole?

options.text: Ergot agonists rarely used because of toxicity; cause livedo reticularis
MAO-B inhibitors that improve on/off fluctuations
Non-ergot dopamine agonists; toxicity includes nausea, impulse control disorder, postural hypotension, and hallucinations
Antimuscarinics that improve tremor more than bradykinesia
COMT inhibitors that prevent peripheral L-DOPA degradation

explanation_correct: Non-ergot dopamine agonists (pramipexole, ropinirole) are preferred in younger patients with Parkinson disease. Their toxicity includes nausea, impulse control disorders (eg, gambling), postural hypotension, hallucinations, confusion, sleepiness, and edema. The ergot bromocriptine is rarely used because of toxicity.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bromocriptine is the ergot agonist; livedo reticularis is a toxicity of amantadine.
explanation_incorrect.B: MAO-B inhibitors are selegiline and rasagiline.
explanation_incorrect.D: The antimuscarinics are benztropine and trihexyphenidyl.
explanation_incorrect.E: COMT inhibitors are entacapone and tolcapone.

educationalObjective: Non-ergot dopamine agonists are preferred in younger patients but can cause impulse control disorder, hallucinations, and postural hypotension.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 62-year-old woman with Parkinson disease on levodopa develops troublesome levodopa-induced dyskinesias. Her neurologist adds a drug that increases dopamine release and decreases dopamine reuptake. After starting it she develops a net-like purplish discoloration of her legs and ankle edema.
question: Which drug is most likely responsible for these findings?
explanation_correct: Amantadine increases dopamine release and decreases dopamine reuptake and is mainly used to reduce levodopa-induced dyskinesias. Its toxicity includes peripheral edema, livedo reticularis, and ataxia. This patient's livedo reticularis and edema point directly to amantadine.

explanation_incorrect.B: Selegiline is an MAO-B inhibitor used for on/off fluctuations; it does not cause livedo reticularis.
explanation_incorrect.C: Benztropine is an antimuscarinic used for tremor and rigidity.
explanation_incorrect.D: Entacapone is a peripheral COMT inhibitor used with levodopa.
explanation_incorrect.E: Pramipexole is a dopamine agonist whose toxicity includes impulse control disorder and hallucinations, not livedo reticularis.

educationalObjective: Amantadine increases dopamine availability, reduces levodopa-induced dyskinesias, and causes livedo reticularis and edema.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A patient with Parkinson disease on levodopa experiences wearing-off between doses. His neurologist adds entacapone. The student reviewing the case notes that this drug acts outside the brain to prevent the peripheral conversion of L-DOPA to 3-O-methyldopa, thereby increasing the amount of L-DOPA entering the CNS.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of entacapone?

options.text: Central COMT inhibition blocking conversion of dopamine to 3-methoxytyramine
Selective MAO-B inhibition in the brain
Peripheral COMT inhibition preventing L-DOPA degradation to 3-O-methyldopa

explanation_correct: Entacapone and tolcapone prevent peripheral L-DOPA degradation to 3-O-methyldopa (3-OMD) by inhibiting COMT and are used with levodopa to increase CNS L-DOPA availability. Tolcapone also crosses the BBB and inhibits central COMT, blocking conversion of dopamine to 3-methoxytyramine. Carbidopa, by contrast, inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase.

explanation_incorrect.A: Central COMT inhibition blocking conversion of dopamine to 3-MT describes tolcapone's central action, not entacapone's peripheral action.
explanation_incorrect.B: MAO-B inhibition is the mechanism of selegiline and rasagiline.
explanation_incorrect.C: Peripheral DOPA decarboxylase inhibition is the mechanism of carbidopa.
explanation_incorrect.E: Vesicular monoamine transporter inhibition is the mechanism of tetrabenazine.

educationalObjective: Entacapone inhibits peripheral COMT, preventing L-DOPA conversion to 3-OMD and increasing CNS L-DOPA delivery.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 65-year-old man with Parkinson disease notices cyclic fluctuations in his levodopa efficacy, with good mobility during 'on' periods and poor function during 'off' periods. His physician adds an agent that acts centrally to block the breakdown of dopamine to DOPAC by selectively inhibiting an enzyme that is more abundant in the brain than in the periphery.
question: Which drug acts by this mechanism?
explanation_correct: Selegiline and rasagiline selectively inhibit MAO-B, which is more common in the brain than the periphery, blocking conversion of dopamine to DOPAC. They are used to improve symptoms in patients with cyclic fluctuations in levodopa efficacy (the on/off phenomenon).

explanation_incorrect.A: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase and cannot cross the BBB.
explanation_incorrect.D: Amantadine increases dopamine release and decreases reuptake.
explanation_incorrect.E: Benztropine is an antimuscarinic for tremor and rigidity.

educationalObjective: Selegiline/rasagiline inhibit brain MAO-B, blocking dopamine breakdown to DOPAC and improving on/off fluctuations.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 55-year-old woman with Parkinson disease has a prominent resting tremor and rigidity but relatively little bradykinesia. Her physician prescribes an antimuscarinic agent to curb excess cholinergic activity, noting that it improves tremor and rigidity but has minimal effect on bradykinesia.
question: Which of the following drugs is most appropriate for this patient?
explanation_correct: Benztropine and trihexyphenidyl are antimuscarinic agents that improve tremor and rigidity in Parkinson disease but have little effect on bradykinesia. They are most useful when tremor and rigidity predominate, as in this patient.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pramipexole is a dopamine agonist with a broad range of effects and distinct toxicities, not an antimuscarinic.
explanation_incorrect.B: Levodopa addresses bradykinesia and all cardinal features, but the scenario specifically asks for an antimuscarinic.
explanation_incorrect.C: Amantadine is used mainly to reduce levodopa-induced dyskinesias.
explanation_incorrect.D: Selegiline is an MAO-B inhibitor used for on/off fluctuations.

educationalObjective: Benztropine/trihexyphenidyl are antimuscarinics that improve tremor and rigidity but not bradykinesia in Parkinson disease.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 38-year-old man and a 75-year-old man are both newly diagnosed with Parkinson disease. Initial treatment strategy differs by age: non-ergot dopamine agonists are preferred in younger patients, whereas levodopa/carbidopa is preferred in older patients. Deep brain stimulation of the STN or GPi can aid advanced disease.
question: Which of the following best reflects the recommended initial strategy for the younger patient?

options.text: Levodopa/carbidopa, because it is preferred in younger patients
Bromocriptine, an ergot agonist preferred for its favorable toxicity profile
A non-ergot dopamine agonist such as pramipexole or ropinirole

explanation_correct: The most effective treatments for Parkinson disease are non-ergot dopamine agonists (preferred in younger patients) and levodopa/carbidopa (preferred in older patients). Deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus aids advanced disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Levodopa/carbidopa is preferred in older patients, not younger ones.
explanation_incorrect.B: Bromocriptine is an ergot agonist rarely used because of toxicity.
explanation_incorrect.D: Tetrabenazine is a VMAT inhibitor used for Huntington chorea and tardive dyskinesia.
explanation_incorrect.E: Riluzole reduces glutamate excitotoxicity and is used for ALS.

educationalObjective: Non-ergot dopamine agonists are preferred in younger Parkinson patients; levodopa/carbidopa in older patients.
